title: Machine-learning screening guides ionic-liquid polymer electrolytes for lithium-metal batteries
summary: A machine-learning and quantum-chemistry workflow screened ionic liquids for conductivity and electrochemical-window properties, then guided selection for rigid-rod polyelectrolyte membranes. The 2022 preprint reports ~50 μm membranes and lithium-cell testing, including symmetric-cell cycling up to 800 hours at room temperature and reversible operation at 6 mA cm−2 at 80°C. Its preprint abstract reports 146 mAh g−1 at 5C/80°C; the later 2023 journal abstract lists 3C, so those version-specific figures are not conflated.
ai_technology: Graph-convolutional neural network and ensemble SVM/random-forest/XGBoost screening with Psi4 quantum-chemistry descriptors

evidence.tested: The 2022 preprint reports a machine-learning/quantum-chemistry workflow that screened 2,356 ion pairs and recommended 40 for testing in rigid-rod polyelectrolyte membranes. It reports symmetric-cell cycling up to 800 hours at room temperature and reversible operation at 6 mA cm−2 at 80°C; its abstract reports 146 mAh g−1 at 5C/80°C.
evidence.unknown: The 2023 journal abstract reports the same study but gives 146 mAh g−1 at 3C rather than 5C. The record keeps the version-specific preprint metric separate and does not transfer it to the journal version. A publisher correction changes plot labels, not the core study claim.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning models and quantum-chemistry calculations screened ionic-liquid properties and guided selection for experimental polymer-electrolyte membranes and cell testing.

source_review.scope: Primary Research Square v1 full-text PDF, including version date, affiliations, Methods and Results; primary Nature Communications journal article indexed text and metadata; primary publisher correction notice.
